s1.syndrome_frame: A chronic, pruritic rash with firm, red-brown plaques on the proximal upper extremities and anterior trunk in a patient with a history of systemic sclerosis
salient_findings: Firm, red-brown plaques without overlying scale on the proximal upper extremities and anterior trunk
Nodular proliferations of thick collagen fibers in large fascicles on lesional punch biopsy
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 60s
Patient has a history of systemic sclerosis
Patient has a history of heart failure, interstitial lung disease, sclerodactyly, and Raynaud phenomenon
Patient is receiving mycophenolate mofetil, 1 g twice daily
Rash is pruritic and has been present for 3 months
Patient denied any known preceding triggers or trauma to the area of the rash
Review of systems was negative for any new or worsening constitutional, respiratory, or gastrointestinal symptoms
Complete blood cell count with differential was unremarkable
Tissue cultures obtained by punch biopsy were negative for bacteria, fungus, and acid-fast bacillus

shortlist.label: Scleromyxedema
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's rash and history of systemic sclerosis, along with the presence of firm, red-brown plaques and nodular proliferations of thick collagen fibers, are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic fasciitis
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's symptoms, including a pruritic rash and the presence of homogeneous, brightly eosinophilic collagen bundles in haphazard array on biopsy, are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Nephrogenic systemic fibrosis
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's history of systemic sclerosis and the presence of firm, red-brown plaques are consistent with this diagnosis, although the absence of renal failure in the case context makes it less likely

shortlist.label: Morphea
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's symptoms, including a pruritic rash and the presence of firm, red-brown plaques, are consistent with this diagnosis, although the lack of skin tightening in the affected areas makes it less likely

shortlist.label: Lichen sclerosus
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's symptoms, including a pruritic rash and the presence of firm, red-brown plaques, are consistent with this diagnosis, although the lack of characteristic histological features makes it less likely

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of firm, red-brown plaques without overlying scale, along with the histopathological findings of nodular proliferations of thick collagen fibers and homogeneous, brightly eosinophilic collagen bundles, is consistent with scleromyxedema. The patient's history of systemic sclerosis and the absence of other explanations for the rash also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Eosinophilic fasciitis
rejected.why: The lack of significant eosinophilia and the presence of nodular plaques are not typical of eosinophilic fasciitis

rejected.label: Nephrogenic systemic fibrosis
rejected.why: There is no mention of renal failure or exposure to gadolinium-based contrast agents, which are typical risk factors for nephrogenic systemic fibrosis

rejected.label: Morphea
rejected.why: The presence of nodular plaques and the histopathological findings are not typical of morphea, which usually presents with sclerotic plaques

rejected.label: Lichen sclerosus
rejected.why: The clinical and histopathological findings do not match lichen sclerosus, which typically presents with white, atrophic plaques and a different histological appearance
